description: One GPS fix, taken during a shift, at a time. A breadcrumb rather than a position: the shift already has a location in the words the crew uses and a coordinate for the weather fetch, and neither of those answers where the crew actually went between six in the morning and three in the afternoon. A track does, and it is the same evidence twice over — which block the crew was in when the re-entry interval was running, and whether the hours somebody is claiming were worked where the work was. NOT A CHILD TABLE OF THE SHIFT, deliberately: a nine-hour shift logging a fix every two minutes is two hundred and seventy rows, and a child table is loaded whole every time anybody opens the shift form. Rows are appended and never edited; a breadcrumb somebody could correct is not a record of where the phone was.

fields.description: The shift this fix was taken during. Required: a coordinate with no exposure period behind it is a dot on a map, and every question this doctype exists to answer — which block, during which hours, under whose supervision — is asked of a shift.
fields.label: Shift

fields.description: Whose phone this came off, when the fix belongs to one person rather than to the crew. Optional on purpose: a foreman's phone in the truck traces the crew's day, and refusing that fix because it names nobody in particular would throw away the only track most shifts will ever have.
fields.label: Employee

fields.description: Denormalised from the Employee at write time, so a track read years later still names the person as they were named then.
fields.label: Employee Name

fields.description: Filled from the shift on save. It is what scopes a track to a company — a User Permission on Company reaches this doctype because this column links to one, and without it a scoped account could read every crew's movements on the site.
fields.label: Company

fields.description: When the fix was taken, which is not when it arrived. A phone out of signal in a canyon posts an hour of breadcrumbs the moment it comes back, and a timestamp assigned on receipt would draw the crew's whole morning at the spot where the bars returned.
fields.label: Timestamp

fields.description: Where the fix came from. iOS is the ordinary case — the phone posting periodically while the shift is open. Manual is somebody typing a coordinate afterwards, and it is a different kind of evidence: worth keeping, worth being able to tell apart.
fields.label: Source

fields.description: Decimal degrees, -90 to 90. Seven decimal places is about a centimetre — far finer than any phone fixes, and here so a coordinate is stored as it arrived rather than rounded on the way in.
fields.label: Latitude

fields.description: Decimal degrees, -180 to 180. Negative in the western hemisphere: a Pacific Northwest orchard reads about -121, and a positive number there is a coordinate in China.
fields.label: Longitude

fields.description: The horizontal accuracy the phone reported, in metres. KEPT RATHER THAN USED AS A GATE: a fix under trees in a canyon reads badly and is still the only record that the crew was there, and a threshold that dropped it would delete the evidence from exactly the ground that is hardest to work. It is here so a reader can weigh a breadcrumb — a 5-metre fix and a 300-metre fix are both true and they are not the same claim.
fields.label: Accuracy (metres)

fields.description: Computed. The H3 cell this point falls in at resolution 10, so a track can be joined against a Field's or a Parcel's stored coverage without loading either polygon. Blank on a site without the h3 package; the coordinates are the record and this is the index.
fields.label: H3 Cell (res 10)

fields.description: Why this fix is here, for the ones somebody entered by hand. Empty for everything the phone posted.
fields.label: Notes

name: Shift Location Log
